verdict.rationale: Turso markets libSQL as 'fully backwards compatible with SQLite' [turso-docs-24, turso-docs-30], but hands-on community reports document concrete dialect/compatibility gaps: missing savepoints, window functions, and ATTACH DATABASE support [turso-comm-9], unimplemented conflict resolution [turso-comm-12], WAL-mode locking behavior differing from real SQLite [turso-comm-4], and file-format compatibility breaking once Turso extensions are used—breaking SQLite CLI, Litestream, sqlite_rsync, and recovery tools [turso-comm-8]. This is a genuine SQLite-family engine (not Postgres/MySQL), so the story only partially applies, and even within that scope real developers report it diverging from a true SQLite superset rather than being fully compatible. Missing for 10: independent verification of Postgres/MySQL wire-protocol support (not offered), and resolution/acknowledgment of the specific missing SQL features reported by users.
